has_subtypes.description: A regulatory MSUD form caused by loss of the PPM1K-encoded PP2Cm phosphatase that normally activates BCKDH. The reported patient had a homozygous truncating variant associated with chromosome 4 uniparental isodisomy. This molecular subtype is not synonymous with every clinically mild MSUD presentation.

evidence.explanation: Identifies the homozygous PPM1K lesion in the reported mild MSUD case.
evidence.reference_title: A novel regulatory defect in the branched-chain α-keto acid dehydrogenase complex due to a mutation in the PPM1K gene causes a mild variant phenotype of maple syrup urine disease.
evidence.snippet: Mutation analysis of the candidate gene, PPM1K, revealed a homozygous c.417_418delTA change predicted to result in a truncated, unstable protein.

evidence.explanation: Complementation in patient fibroblasts supports a causal regulatory defect.
evidence.reference_title: A novel regulatory defect in the branched-chain α-keto acid dehydrogenase complex due to a mutation in the PPM1K gene causes a mild variant phenotype of maple syrup urine disease.
evidence.snippet: The transient expression of wild-type PPM1K in PP2Cm-deficient fibroblasts recovered 35% of normal BCKDH activity.

omimps_mappings.mapping_justification: The January 2026 series contains BCKDHA-, BCKDHB-, DBT- and PPM1K-related records plus the broader DLD deficiency record OMIM:246900. This entry models the MSUD phenotype, including the PPM1K regulatory form, and discusses a BCKDK-associated biochemical phenotype not separately enumerated in this snapshot. DLD affects other dehydrogenase complexes as well as BCKDH; its full clinical scope is not a subtype of isolated MSUD. RelatedMatch records this overlap without equating all DLD deficiency with MSUD or treating the series as an exhaustive list of regulatory causes.
